messages.subject: Modify the iterations
parts:
Hi
Can I change or fix the number of iterations in the lavaan´s measurementInvariance function?
The model didn´t converge for the strong invariance and I want to try more iterations

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Modify the iterations
parts:
On 02/20/2014 04:59 PM, joe doggy wrote:
> Hi
> Can I change or fix the number of iterations in the lavaan´s
> measurementInvariance function?
> The model didn´t converge for the strong invariance and I want to try
> more iterations

You can fit the 'strong invariance' model on itself (using cfa/sem,
instead of the measurementInvariance function), and then you have access
to all the arguments of the optimizer via the control() argument (see
?nlminb for an overview).

For example, changing the maximum number of iterations to, say, 5:

fit <- cfa(HS.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939, control=list(iter.max=5))

The default value for iter.max is 10000. So, increasing this number will
not help you. If the model estimates look ok (eg no negative variances),
but the model did not converge, you may try to relax the convergence
criteria, for example:

fit <- cfa(HS.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939,
control=list(rel.tol=1e-4))

Another option may be to provide better starting values. If everything
fails, and you believe it should converge, please send me your full R
script + a snippet of the data.

Yves.
